sections.heading: DK Milk Union: Mangaluru's Co-operative Dairy
paragraphs: The Dakshina Kannada Co-operative Milk Producers' Union (DKMUL) was registered on 8 May 1986 and covers the coastal Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts. It grew out of the Canara Milk Union started at Manipal in 1974, and today records 730 functioning village dairy societies and 146,127 farmer members, 45,772 of them women.

DairyNews, citing The Hindu, reported in April 2026 that DKMUL's average daily collection in 2025-26 rose 19 per cent to 4.07 lakh litres, that it still brings in about 40,000 litres a day from other unions, that business volume reached Rs 1,270 crore, and that KMF products make up 73 per cent of the milk and milk products sold in Mangaluru and nearby areas.

sections.heading: Mangalore Dairy at Kulshekar and Its UHT Block
paragraphs: The union's Mangalore Dairy stands at Kulshekar. DKMUL's milestones list a 1 lakh litre dairy commissioned there on 10 October 1991, a product plant in 1994, a sterilised flavoured milk plant in 2007 and a modernised dairy inaugurated on 14 February 2009. A flexi-pack and production block opened on 5 April 2016 with the release of Trupti 500 ml UHT milk, followed by a 180 ml pack that November.

DKMUL now lists the Mangalore plant at 2,50,000 litres a day, making ghee, peda, Mysore Pak, lassi, curds, buttermilk, paneer, flavoured milk and UHT milk. The April 2026 report says the Kulashekara dairy is over 30 years old and is to be expanded, with an ice cream plant and a paneer unit also planned.

sections.heading: Udupi Dairy at Uppoor and the Coastal Chilling Network
paragraphs: A second dairy of 2,50,000 litres a day was inaugurated at Uppoor in Udupi district on 29 January 2019, its foundation stone having been laid in April 2017. The union also runs chilling centres at Puttur (30,000 litres a day) and Manipal (50,000 litres a day) and 130 bulk milk coolers out in the villages.

Liquid milk is still the bulk of the business, but cultured and fat products are large too: the 2025-26 figures put average daily sales at 3.87 lakh litres of milk, 81,979 kg of curds, 2.8 tonnes of paneer and 6.1 tonnes of ghee.

sections.heading: Matching Tube Finish to Mangaluru Product Lines
paragraphs: Curd and lassi culturing, UHT and flavoured milk, ghee clarification and the planned ice cream and paneer units leave protein and fat on the tube wall between cleans, so we recommend 316L to ASTM A270 with an SF4 electropolished bore for those runs. Each electropolished lot ships with an Ra report and an EN 10204 3.1 certificate traced to the heat number.
Tanker reception, chilling-centre transfer lines, chilled water and CIP return headers seldom need that finish, and SF1 or mill-finish 304L keeps the cost of a coastal expansion project in check.

sections.heading: What to Send With a Mangaluru Enquiry
bullets: Section the tube is for: reception, curd and lassi, UHT, ghee, ice cream, paneer or CIP

sections.heading: Delivery to Mangaluru, Udupi and Coastal Karnataka
paragraphs: Mangaluru consignments leave Mumbai by road with every electropolished length end-capped and sleeved, and the dispatch date and transit are stated in writing at order confirmation. All lengths are PMI-verified before loading, and a complete enquiry is answered with a quotation inside 24 hours.
